sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The first sh:sparql constraint still violates the prior repair instruction: it selects an applicable pre-cutoff ship merely when deliveryDate, assessmentDate, or engineOutputComplianceMethod is absent, rather than selecting only the actual deadline violation. Remove this redundant constraint, or rewrite it so it selects only an IA/IA Super ship with constructionStageDate before 2003-09-01, permitted compliance method, and assessmentDate later than 1 January of the year twenty years after delivery. Preserve the existing single-valued, xsd:date, cutoff, and controlled-method constraints; post-cutoff ships must not generate a violation.

rows: The conditional query has accidental pass logic for multi-valued properties: it succeeds when any valid construction date, delivery/assessment-date pair, or permitted compliance method exists, while malformed, contradictory, or additional disallowed values are ignored. Constrain these single-valued inputs to the verified cardinality and xsd:date/controlled-value domains, or make the SPARQL checks universal so every supplied value is valid and the applicable deadline comparison cannot be bypassed by another value.

Reverse the polarity of both sh:sparql constraints. In SHACL-SPARQL, selected focus nodes are violations, but the first query currently selects an applicable IA/IA Super ship when its construction date is before 1 September 2003 and its assessment is on or before the deadline—the compliant case—while allowing the noncompliant case to pass. The second query currently selects IA/IA Super ships constructed on or after 1 September 2003—the compliant exception—and therefore rejects them. Rewrite the queries to select only actual violations: for the pre-1-September-2003 applicable case, select when assessmentDate is later than 1 January of the year twenty years after delivery (while requiring the permitted method); for the post-cutoff case, do not select a violation. Preserve the existing single-value, datatype, and controlled-value constraints addressing the prior multi-valued-property feedback.

The first sh:sparql constraint is still an accidental rejection: it selects every ship whose iceClass is IA or IA Super, regardless of construction date, delivery date, assessment date, method, or deadline, so even compliant applicable ships fail and post-cutoff ships are incorrectly rejected. Remove this redundant constraint or rewrite it to select only an actual violation, namely an IA/IA Super ship constructed before 2003-09-01 whose assessmentDate is later than 1 January in the year twenty years after delivery, with the permitted compliance method. Preserve the existing single-valued, xsd:date, cutoff, and controlled-method constraints; the post-cutoff branch must not generate a violation.

The first sh:sparql constraint still violates the prior repair instruction: it selects an applicable pre-cutoff ship merely when deliveryDate, assessmentDate, or engineOutputComplianceMethod is absent, rather than selecting only the actual deadline violation. Remove this redundant constraint, or rewrite it so it selects only an IA/IA Super ship with constructionStageDate before 2003-09-01, permitted compliance method, and assessmentDate later than 1 January of the year twenty years after delivery. Preserve the existing single-valued, xsd:date, cutoff, and controlled-method constraints; post-cutoff ships must not generate a violation.
